interventions.body: Postoperative prognosis depends on the preoperative PSA and the prostatectomy findings. Extraprostatic extension is reported absent. Positive surgical margins is reported absent. Seminal vesicle invasion is reported absent. Lymphovascular invasion is reported absent. No lymph nodes were sampled; pNx does not establish node-negative disease and widens uncertainty. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are needed to refine this prognosis; a future recurrence date cannot be established from surgical risk factors alone. The fixed estimated horizon is 51.41 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 33.42–69.40 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text: The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Favorable findings include a negative surgical margin (0.0), no seminal vesicle invasion (0.0), and absence of lymphovascular invasion (0.0). The pathological stage was pT2 with no extraprostatic extension. Countervailing factors include the preoperative PSA of 18 and the absence of documented nodal sampling, which widens uncertainty regarding true nodal status, as pNx is not equivalent to pN0. The biopsy-to-prostatectomy difference is noted as the Gleason pattern and ISUP report are missing. The current horizon suggests a follow-up period of 51.4088 months without an event. Postoperative PSA and its trajectory are critical missing pieces of information that would significantly revise this assessment. Missing nodal sampling further complicates the certainty of the overall outcome.

The patient underwent a robot-assisted radical prostatectomy with a pathological stage of pT2, negative surgical margins, and no seminal vesicle invasion. The absence of lymph nodes removed is noted, and nodal status is uncertain as no nodes were sampled, which widens the uncertainty. The preoperative PSA was 18. The surgical findings, including Gleason 4+3 (ISUP grade group 3), negative margins, and absence of lymphovascular invasion, are favorable factors. Countervailing findings include the preoperative PSA level and the missing biopsy grade and ISUP report. The prognosis is guided by the surgical findings, but the missing pathological details and the lack of nodal sampling introduce uncertainty. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory is crucial for revising this prognosis. The heuristic horizon suggests a follow-up period of 51.4088 months without an event.
